text:
Kirill Kaprizov leads the NHL with 16 goals, per Field Level Media, rides an eight-game point streak and has 31 points in 19 games. Minnesota's top line of Kaprizov, Matt Boldy and Joel Eriksson Ek is driving the Wild's start: at five on five Minnesota gets 61% of the expected goals (the share of chance quality) with him on the ice.

The chances are better than last season: his individual expected goals sit at 1.87 per 60, up from 1.32, so this isn't only a hot stick. But he's shooting 26%, against 17% last season, with 16 goals on 12.8 expected. That finishing rate rarely lasts even for great shooters; expect the goal pace to cool while the points keep coming.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows how he does it: he carried the puck in on 57% of his entries last season and ranked in the 87th percentile among forwards for primary shot assists. Our projection still has him finishing around 51 goals, in a range from 42 to 61. Quinn Hughes, after the San Jose win: "I just feel like we can tilt the ice when they're out there" (via NHL.com's Heather Rule).
headline: Kirill Kaprizov is leading the league, for now
